source.quote: Hass was the most precocious cultivar, with bearing starting in the second season, and reaching 10 t ha-1 by year three.
source.doc: Wolstenholme, Kaiser & Palmer, 'Yield Potential of Intensively Managed Avocados in the Natal Midlands — The Early Bearing Years', South African Avocado Growers' Association Yearbook 1991, 14:15-18

yearsToFirstCrop.note: Bruyns Hill, Natal Midlands bioclimatic group 2; irrigated Hass on clonal Duke 7 rootstock, 7 x 7 m (200 trees/ha), planted 1982–1984. The paper reports Hass starting in its second season and Fuerte in its third. The two-to-three-year reference describes those trial cultivars, not every avocado or nursery starting age.

source.quote: Hass was the most precocious and consistent bearer, averaging over 15 t ha-1 and reaching an average of 20 t ha-1 by the sixth year. Thereafter, an average yield of about 22,5 t ha-1 appears to be sustainable.

yearsToFullBearing.note: In this irrigated, intensively managed Natal Midlands trial, Hass reached about 20 t/ha at age 6 and orchards approached maximum sustainable average yield by age 8. This is a trial-specific bearing reference; there is no national plateau or automatically interpolated age-yield curve.

source.quote: reaching an average of 20 t ha-1 by the sixth year. Thereafter, an average yield of about 22,5 t ha-1 appears to be sustainable ... At a spacing of 7 x 7 m (200 trees per ha)

yieldKgPerTree.note: Same-trial arithmetic at the initial 200 trees/ha: 20,000 kg/ha / 200 = 100 kg/tree at age 6; sustainable average 22,500 kg/ha / 200 = 112.5 kg/tree. At age 3, 10,000 kg/ha / 200 = 50 kg/tree equivalent. These are average-equivalent reference values for the named Hass/Duke 7 orchard conditions, not measured individual-tree yields or default production for a different density, cultivar, climate or management. Intermediate ages are not inferred.

source.quote: Hass, an A-type flowerer, tended to be out of phase with Fuerte and Rinton on a seasonal yield basis ... favourable temperatures at fruit-set (especially in B flowering type cultivars such as Fuerte) can result in heavy cropping

pollination.note: SA source confirms avocado's type A / type B protogynous dichogamous flowering system (temporal separation of male and female phases within a single tree) rather than stating self-fertility directly. Supporting SA quote on the practical effect: DAFF/ARC 'Cultivation of Avocados' guide lists for Fuerte (a Type B cultivar) 'Comments: fruit set increased by a pollinator' (http://www.avocadosource.com/international/south_africa_papers/cultivation_of_avocados.pdf, p.5), i.e. trees do set fruit alone (self-fertile) but cross-pollination with the opposite flower type improves fruit set — hence 'partly-self-fertile' rather than 'self-fertile' or 'needs-cross-pollinator'.

supplementaryReferences.title: Hass age benchmarks — irrigated Natal Midlands trial

source.doc: Wolstenholme, Kaiser & Palmer (1991), SAAGA Yearbook 14:15–18; reflowed PDF

supplementaryReferences.note: Hass on Duke 7, initially 200 trees/ha at Bruyns Hill (Natal Midlands bioclimatic group 2), with intensive irrigation and nutrition. Age 3: 10,000 kg/ha; age 6: 20,000 kg/ha; sustainable average about 22,500 kg/ha. Same-study density permits equivalents of 50 kg/tree at age 3 and 100 kg/tree at age 6; there is no reference for every intermediate age. These orchard benchmarks are conditional on good resources, comparable climate and timely orchard management, including Phytophthora control and thinning; do not auto-fill farm quantities.
